definition: An early and influential family of models that learned word embeddings from large corpora using shallow neural networks.
details: Word2Vec introduced the continuous bag-of-words (CBOW) and skip-gram objectives, predicting a word from its context or vice versa. Its embeddings captured semantic and syntactic regularities — famously king − man + woman ≈ queen — and demonstrated that cheap, fast models could learn rich word meaning from raw text.
story: Think of an orchestra warming up: no single instrument carries the piece, but together they make the sound. At the bottom of every machine is a design — the shape of it, and how its pieces talk to each other. The layout decides what the machine can even attempt, before it learns a single thing. The shape of the machine is half the idea. And that shape of the machine — Word2Vec — is what makes everything else possible.

citation.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
